articles.title: Predicting Gerrit Cole, Yankees Rotation and Lineups for Wild Card vs. Red Sox
articles.summary: Though nothing is set in stone yet, all signs continue to point toward the New York Yankees hosting the Boston Red Sox in the wild card round of Major League Baseball's postseason for a second consecutive year.
articles.body:
Though nothing is set in stone yet, all signs continue to point toward the New York Yankees hosting the Boston Red Sox in the wild card round of Major League Baseball's postseason for a second consecutive year.

Sure, if the Yankees sweep the four-game set at home against Tampa Bay that begins next Tuesday, they could still win the AL East and avoid playing in the wild card round at all. It's also possible (though extremely unlikely) that Boston collapses so drastically down the stretch that it ends up either as the No. 6 seed or outside the postseason picture altogether.

As of Sunday morning, though, FanDuel had the Yankees at -1100 to earn the AL's No. 4 seed, while Boston appears so locked into the AL's No. 5 seed that it's the only one of the 12 postseason spots on which FanDuel is no longer taking action.

A bracket featuring 4. NYY vs. 5. BOS is so inevitable at this point that we're ready to start projecting the roster that the Yankees will bring into that no-love-lost clash.

Before we can do that, however, how healthy are the Bronx Bombers?

2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. suffered a sprained right thumb in the middle of last week, landing on the IL on Thursday. Bryan Hoch reported that Chisholm "expects to play before the end of the regular season," hoping to return for the season-ending seven-game homestand.

CF Trent Grisham is recovering from a Grade 2 hamstring strain suffered on Sept. 4. Per Yankees beat writer Gary Phillips , manager Aaron Boone said on Sunday it's possible Grisham could return by the end of the regular season, "but he doesn't have a clear timeline yet."

DH Giancarlo Stanton is still hitting in his months-long recovery, but a return to the lineup is nowhere near imminent. He reaggravated his initial right calf injury in June and then injured the left calf when he fell running the bases in August. When the latter occurred, it rather felt like the final straw and that we won't see him again until 2027.

RHP Clarke Schmidt has made five appearances in his rehab from Tommy John surgery, nearing a return to the big leagues as a reliever. Schmidt has struck out 11 of the 26 batters he has faced and could be quite the eleventh-hour solution to the Yankees' eighth inning woes. (4.74 ERA against in the eighth compared to a sub-3.00 ERA in the fifth, sixth, seventh and ninth innings.)

LHP Ryan Weathers has been out for three weeks with a flexor strain in his throwing arm. He has been throwing long toss, though, and they hope to get him throwing off a mound in the coming days. Along with Schmidt, he, too, could factor into the bullpen mix in October.

Yankees Projected Starting Lineups vs. Boston

Provided Chisholm is healthy, the only real question is which direction the Yankees opt to go with the left half of their infield—and whether Anthony Volpe factors into the mix at all.

We can pretty well assume it'll be Goldschmidt leading off against Boston's southpaws, but definitely not starting against Sonny Gray, against whom he is 1-for-26 in his career. Garcia (4-for-10 with one HR off Gray) should be in the cleanup spot for that one and the primary pinch hitter for the other two games.

We can also pretty well assume that Judge and Bellinger will be at Nos. 2 and 3 in the order, even though Judge is just 3-for-17 with nine strikeouts and no extra-base hits since his return from the IL.

McMahon has not hit well at all against lefties this season, but he does have solid career numbers against Suarez (6-for-16 with one home run). If he only starts one game in the series, it might be that one.

Amed Rosario could be an intriguing option in either of the first two games. He is 7-for-24 (.292) in his career against Gray, as well as 5-for-15 (.333) with two home runs and no strikeouts against Suarez. Maybe Boone starts him and saves McMahon as a pinch hitter instead of the other way around.

Yankees Projected Starting Rotation vs. Boston

Indisputable. Not only is he the frontrunner for AL Cy Young and a plausible candidate for AL MVP , but he has eviscerated the Red Sox thus far in his young career. New York will be hoping for a repeat of his 8.0 IP, 0 R, 12 K masterpiece from Game 3 of last year's wild card series.

If he's physically good to go for up to 100 pitches, this one also should be relatively indisputable. Since signing with the Yankees, Fried has made six starts (including Game 1 last year) against Boston, owning the Red Sox to the tune of a 1.24 ERA and a 10.2 K/9.

Gerrit Cole is one of the highest-paid pitchers on the planet, and he hasn't missed a single turn through the rotation since making his season debut in late May.

However, he has been getting shelled as of late, allowing seven home runs over his last two starts, saddled with a 6.48 ERA (and a 7.30 FIP) thus far in September.

Even if you're inclined to disregard that recent rough patch and just ride with the 2023 Cy Young winner in a do-or-die situation, there's also this:

Gerrit Cole vs. Boston (regular seasons 2021-26) : 75.0 IP, 6.36 ERA Gerrit Cole vs. Boston (postseason career) : 8.0 IP, 7.88 ERA

Gerrit Cole vs. Not-Boston (regular seasons 2021-26) : 726.1 IP, 2.90 ERA Gerrit Cole vs. Not-Boston (postseason career) : 125.1 IP, 2.44 ERA

Schlittler and Fried have owned the Red Sox, but Boston has had Cole's number since long before his recent schneid began.

The dream scenario, of course, is that there is no Game 3 and that Cole instead toes the rubber in Game 1 of the ALDS in Tampa Bay—against whom he has made four career postseason starts with a 1.66 ERA.

If there is a Game 3, though, Rodón and his 2.25 ERA over the past month should be the way to go.

If Boone has the courage to go that route and the Yankees get eliminated without Cole ever throwing a pitch in three games, surely the responses will be calm, cool and collected, right?

articles.title: Yankees Address Legionella Bacteria Found in Stadium Cooling Tower amid Investigation for Outbreak
articles.summary: The New York Yankees said there's no connection between the cases of Legionnaires' disease in the Bronx and the bacteria that was discovered in a cooling tower at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees said there's no connection between the cases of Legionnaires' disease in the Bronx and the bacteria that was discovered in a cooling tower at Yankee Stadium.

"No current cases have been associated with Yankee Stadium," the team said, per the Associated Press . "Additionally, the New York City Department of Health has not at any point this month asked us to postpone our games."

The city's health department confirmed there have been 10 positive cases of Legionnaires' disease, with one death and three people hospitalized.

The city said Sunday health department officials tested cooling towers throughout the Bronx. Ten were flagged as testing positive for Legionella bacteria. The results didn't indicate whether the bacteria were alive or dead or whether the sites led to any exposure.

Yankee Stadium was one of the locations impacted. The Yankees told the AP they had their cooling tower drained and cleaned Sunday morning.

The Bronx Bombers wrapped up a six-game home stand later that day with a 2-0 win over the New York Mets.

The team has a pair of road series against the Minnesota Twins and Arizona Diamondbacks before returning to the Bronx on Sept. 22.

The city of New York advised residents to be diligent in the wake of the ongoing situation.

"Any New Yorkers who currently live or work in this area or people who have visited the area since late August and are experiencing flu-like symptoms, such as fever, cough, or difficulty breathing, should contact a healthcare provider immediately," the city said. "Legionnaires' disease is deadly but can be effectively treated if diagnosed early."

The 2026 MLB postseason is right around the corner. And with two weeks left in the regular season, every team with World Series aspirations still has a lot left to play for.

Who has clinched a spot in the playoffs?

The Tampa Bay Rays clinched their postseason berth with a walk-off win over the Astros on Friday. They have not yet secured their seed.

The Milwaukee Brewers clinched their postseason berth with a 20-0 victory over the Reds on Friday. They have not yet secured their seed.

The Yankees' and Dodgers' magic numbers to clinch a postseason berth are down to 1.

On the NL side, the Dodgers, Braves, Phillies and Cubs all have playoff odds above 97%, according to FanGraphs . The Brewers, Braves and Dodgers are in position to win their divisions, while the Cubs currently hold the top wild card.

In the AL, the Yankees and Red Sox have playoff odds of 99% or better. Also in playoff position are the Astros, White Sox and Guardians. The Rays, White Sox and Astros currently lead their divisions, with the Yankees, Red Sox and Guardians making up the wild-card field.

But there's still a lot up for grabs in the wild-card race, as the Blue Jays and Rangers are within two games of the final spot in the AL, and the Diamondbacks are within 2.5 games of the final spot in the NL.

Once a team clinches its ticket to the postseason, there's still a lot to play for . Beyond division leads and wild cards, teams could be battling for playoff positioning until the final game of the regular season.

The Nos. 1 and 2 seeds in each league go to the division winners with the two best records. Those teams earn a bye through the wild-card round and hosting rights in the division series. Currently, the Rays, White Sox, Brewers and Dodgers are in line to claim those seeds.

The No. 3 seeds go to the third division winners — right now that's the Astros and Braves — and those teams will host three-game wild-card series against the No. 6 seeds (which go to the third wild cards). The top wild-card teams in each league — currently the Yankees and Cubs — earn the No. 4 seeds and will host the No. 5 seeds (the second wild cards) in the wild-card round.

The higher seed also gets home-field advantage in the championship series, once we get that far.

articles.title: Why NL exec believes Red Sox are in 'best position' to win AL championship
articles.summary: There are a few key players behind why the Red Sox can make a deep run this year.
articles.body:
The 2026 season for the Boston Red Sox has been quite a wild ride, and heading towards October and postseason baseball, things could get a whole lot stranger.

For this Red Sox squad, there's reason to believe that they can not only make the postseason and win a series or two, but actually win the American League Championship Series. But how?

ESPN's Jesse Rogers shared that one NL executive believes the Red Sox are "best positioned" to win the AL among the Wild Card teams thanks to their elite rotation and elite bullpen.

Red Sox pitching staff is reason why they're 'best positioned' to make surprise run

"I like the amount of arms the Red Sox can put out there in a playoff series," an NL executive said. "And then once you get to the back of a game, they're lights out with [Garrett] Whitlock and Chapman. I think they're best positioned to win from the wild-card teams. They'll keep the Yankees in the park when they play in the first round."

Boston's offense isn't as bad as it seemed earlier in the year, thanks to Roman Anthony 's return, Adley Rutschman 's trade, and the unexpected breakout of Mickey Gasper , among others.

But the real star of the show is their pitching staff. Just looking at the starting rotation, it's a group that has a real chance of holding teams down come the postseason.

Sonny Gray has a 2.76 ERA this season, Ranger Suarez is one of the best postseason pitchers in MLB history, Payton Tolle has been a breakout pitcher, and even Jake Bennett has had his moments. Patrick Sandoval is the fifth starter and won't be needed in October.

Looking to the bullpen, Garrett Whitlock and Aroldis Chapman are a great duo, and with Erik Miller, Bryan Bello, and plenty of other options in a strong bullpen, this pitching staff has more than enough to shut teams down come October.

So, why are the Red Sox "best positioned" among the wild card teams to make a deep postseason run? Their elite pitching staff, both in the rotation and bullpen, should present a huge advantage for the team going forward.

articles.body:
It is time for our updated 2026 MLB Power Rankings ! The regular season may be winding down, but many postseason races are heating up. Both the American League and National League still have multiple teams competing for the final Wild Card spots. Meanwhile, multiple division races are far from decided. One team that is pulling away from the New York Yankees and the rest of the American League are the Tampa Bay Rays, who clinched a postseason spot last week .

The Rays are among the ball clubs who climbed our MLB Power Rankings this week.

The 93-57 Brewers continue to lead the way. The 90-59 Los Angeles Dodgers are still competing for the best record in baseball, but this Brewers ball club is currently the best team in the game.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

LA is poised for another deep postseason run. Regardless of whether or not they surpass the Brewers for the best record, the Dodgers will enter the postseason with confidence. They are playing well and expect to reach the World Series for a third consecutive year.

The Rays are the first 90-win team in the American League this year. They hold a four-game lead over the New York Yankees for both the best record in the AL and the AL East standings. Superstar Junior Caminero and this Tampa Bay ball club have a clear path to reaching the World Series in 2026.

The Braves are just 5-5 over their past 10 games. Nevertheless, Atlanta holds a five-game lead over the Philadelphia Phillies in the NL East.

As mentioned, the Yankees are trailing the Rays in the AL East. New York has the second best record in the AL and the ball club leads the AL Wild Card race.

The Cubs and Phillies are tied for the NL Wild Card lead. For now, Chicago remains ahead of Philadelphia in our MLB Power Rankings, but things could look different next week.

This Phillies ball club is chasing the Braves for the NL East lead. They are poised to reach the postseason as an NL Wild Card team at the very least.

Boston holds the No. 2 spot in the AL Wild Card race. The Red Sox are hoping to get a number of players back from injury ahead of the postseason. They could be a sneaky team to watch in the playoffs.

The Padres and Arizona Diamondbacks have been going back and forth for the final NL Wild Card spot for weeks, but San Diego is beginning to pull away. The Padres are currently 2.5 games ahead of the Diamondbacks for the position. There is still work to do, but San Diego is in a good position. A seven-game winning streak has helped the Padres over the past week.

The Diamondbacks have dropped two consecutive contests while the Padres are continuing their aforementioned winning streak. Arizona still has time to get back on track, but the ball club needs to begin winning consistently while hoping that San Diego's winning streak comes to an end sooner rather than later.

The White Sox's lead over the Cleveland Guardians for first place in the AL Central is suddenly only a half-game. Cleveland happens to be hosting Chicago for a three-game series beginning on Monday. This series could go a long way toward determining the winner of the division.

The Guardians are 6-4 over their past 10 games and are close to surpassing the White Sox in the AL Central as mentioned. They need to get the job done at home this week in their three-game series against the White Sox.

The Astros' lead over the Texas Rangers in the AL West is just one game. Houston has dropped three consecutive contests, so this team needs to turn things around as soon as possible.

The Blue Jays remain only one game back in the AL Wild Card race. Toronto has won two consecutive games and will look to keep the momentum trending in the right direction this week.

The Pirates are climbing the MLB Power Rankings. The problem is that they play in the competitive National League. Pittsburgh is 6.5 games back of an NL Wild Card spot at the moment.

The Marlins have not had the best past couple of weeks, but this team continues to remain around the .500 mark. Miami has displayed potential despite its overall mediocre campaign.

The Cardinals are also hovering around the .500 mark. They will look to finish the 2026 season strong.

Texas is only one game behind Houston for the lead in the AL West. The Rangers have been close to surpassing the Astros for a while, but accomplishing the feat has been difficult for the ball club.

The Orioles are still technically in contention, but they are four games back of the final AL Wild Card spot. Baltimore is just 3-7 over its past 10 contests.

Elly De La Cruz has emerged as an NL MVP candidate. While he won't win the award given the presences of Pete Crow-Armstrong and Shohei Ohtani , De La Cruz's performance has been a bright spot in what has been an otherwise disappointing season for the Reds.

The Twins continue to fall out of contention. It was recently revealed that Byron Buxton will undergo hip surgery. He is hoping to be ready for 2027 spring training, which is encouraging.

The Nationals' strong offense hasn't been enough to keep them in contention this year. They are a few good pitchers away from becoming a contender, though.

It seems like I write the same thing in almost every MLB Power Rankings about the Mariners. They entered the season with lofty expectations but have been one of the biggest disappointments in the game. Nothing has changed for the 70-80 Mariners this week.

The Tigers have won four consecutive contests. They are not a contender at this point, but Detroit can still finish the season strong.

The Mets have played respectable baseball in recent weeks despite their overall underwhelming season. They are 7-3 over their past 10 games.

The Royals have failed to meet expectations in 2026. With that being said, their young core of players suggests they could compete as soon as next year.

The Giants need to figure out their franchise direction. Rebuilding may be their best decision.

The Athletics are similar to the Royals. They expected to play better this year but still feature a quality young core of players. The A's are another team that could compete next season.

The Angels, meanwhile, are similar to the Giants. They need to enter a rebuild, which, to their credit, they began at this year's MLB trade deadline. For now, they remain near the bottom of our MLB Power Rankings.

The Rockies are another team that simply needs to figure out a franchise direction. There isn't much reason to believe they will compete anytime soon despite their year of rebuilding.
